newsitem.title: CANADA: WCE adds oats delivery sites, eyes hog futures.
newsitem.headline: WCE adds oats delivery sites, eyes hog futures.

text.p: Cargill Inc elevators in Duluth and Minneapolis, Minn., will be added to the Winnipeg Commodity Exchange's oats futures contract as delivery points, WCE product development director John DePape told reporters.
"Cargill applied for elevator delivery in Duluth and Minneapolis," DePape said.
The redesigned oat futures contract currently allows for delivery basis rail track Minneapolis but in-store elevator delivery will be added to the March 1997 and subsequent contracts, he said.
About 90 percent of Canadian oat exports go to the United States.
ConAgra Inc is considering allowing delivery at its Minnesota elevators, DePape said.

The WCE also planned to do do a feasibility study of a hog futures contract with the assistance of Memphis-based analytical firm Sparks Companies Inc, WCE trading and markets director Stan Cassar said.
WCE officials consulted hog producers, processors and retailers in Montreal, Toronto, Winnipeg and Edmonton in August to explore whether there was sufficient interest.
"There tended to be broad, general support. They're looking for a reduction in basis risk," Cassar said.
Canadians who trade Chicago Mercantile Exchange hog futures must also hedge their risk on the exchange between Canadian and U.S. dollars, he said.
Another selling point for a Canadian hog futures contract would be specifications that would take superior Canadian hog genetics into account, Cassar said.
"We hope it would attract a cross section of participants. Definitely, there are a lot of American packers taking Canadian hogs who could use this," he added.
The feasibility study will examine estimated trading volume, cost-to-revenue ratio and a hog index price.
Results should be ready within eight weeks, he said.
Sparks also reviewed viability of the WCE's feed barley futures contract in the event western Canadian feed barley is removed from the Canadian Wheat Board's export monopoly.
"Sparks Companies conclusion is the current contract will function appropriately in an open market," DePape said.

A federal export review panel suggested removing feed barley from the CWB mandate. Canada's Agriculture Minister Ralph Goodale has said he plans to announce his intentions in Regina, Saskatchewan, Friday at 1200 EDT/1600 GMT.
